summary: No reachable vulnerabilities. Untrusted input is the stored IndexedDB records. trendData() runs every hand through parseHandRecord and every session through parseSessionRecord inside a per-record try/catch, so malformed or tampered records are skipped and cannot crash the read. Validation is strict: sessionId must match /^[0-9a-f]{32}$/, handNumber must be a whole number >= 1, completedAt/startedAt must round-trip through toISOString (so Date.parse cannot be NaN in orderHands), and decisions are bounded through actions (MAX_ACTIONS). That keeps unhintedMajors, majorPer100 and the SVG coordinates finite and bounded. Every string that reaches the DOM (totals, aria-label, <title>, messages) is built from numbers and constants and rendered as React text or attributes. No dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and stored strings never reach markup (sessionId is used only as a sort key). The read is one read-only transaction with two getAll calls, an O(n) parse and an O(n log n) sort: linear in the user's own local data, with no regex or quadratic hotspots (countText's regex runs only on short numeric strings). The error path logs the error object to the console only, which holds no secrets. No new dependencies, network calls, auth or randomness.
